5.text: The owners of the lakes, rivers, and sea-bays, have an aversion to iron.

6.text: If, in fishing or sealing, any iron tool is dropped into the water, the catch

7.text: will be immediately cut off. The same belief exists among the Russianized

8.text: Yukaghir. It is forbidden to kill a living fish fresh from the water with an

9.text: iron weapon. It is forbidden to kill the eagle and a sea-bird of the species

10.text: of Synthliborhamphus antiquus Gm. The killing of an eagle brings storm;

11.text: and the killing of the other species, fog. The birds of this latter species,

12.text: however, may be killed singly from time to time. When a mother-bird with

13.text: her little ones is met by a hunter, he may kill the latter, but he must immedi-

14.text: ately take to flight, lest the mother-bird revenge on him the death of her

15.text: young. If she gives pursuit, he must show her a talisman in the shape of

16.text: a dried carcass of a bird of the same species, which is often carried for this

17.text: purpose on the boat. Then she will be frightened, and will desist from

18.text: pursuit. The bodies of young birds killed under such conditions may serve

19.text: as amulets, insuring luck in sea-hunting. With the appearance of shot-guns

20.text: bought from the Americans, the taboo against this bird became less strict,

21.text: because the bird-hunters simply shoot down anything that flies by. Notwith-

32.text: Among both the Reindeer and the Maritime people it is forbidden to

33.text: throw away crumbs and remnants of food. The Reindeer people connect it

34.text: with success in reindeer-breeding; for instance, they say that, if a reindeer-

35.text: bone is not entirely gnawed up, the reindeer will be stricken with some

36.text: disease. If the same thing happens with a bone of a leg, the herd will be

37.text: visited by hoof-disease, etc. Therefore housewives gather carefully all

38.text: remnants of food, especially bones, and burn them in the fire. The Maritime
